title: Restriction along colour-equivalent operadic approximations
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and inner, cartesian and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. An infinity operad here is an inner fibration $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ with cocartesian lifts of inert pointed maps, whose colour projections give the fibre-product and mapping-space product Segal axioms: the fibre over $\langle n\rangle$ is equivalent to the $n$-fold product of the fibre over $\langle1\rangle$, and mapping spaces over a pointed map split as products over its non-basepoint outputs. A pointed map is inert if each non-basepoint output has exactly one preimage, and active if only the basepoint maps to the basepoint. Inert edges of $P$ are the $p$-cocartesian edges over inert maps. The nerves $L$ and $A$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], with the pointed-set forgetful map, are instances of this convention.

For a categorical fibration $f:C\to P$, say that $f$ is an approximation if (i) for every $c$ above $\langle n\rangle$ and every colour projection $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$, there exists an edge $c\to c_i$ locally cocartesian for $pf$ over $\rho_i$ whose image in $P$ is inert; and (ii) every active edge $z\to f(c)$ in $P$ has an $f$-cartesian lift with target $c$. Here locally cocartesian means cocartesian in the pullback over the specified edge. A general coherent functor $f:C\to P$ is an approximation if it factors as a categorical equivalence $C\to C'$ followed by a categorical fibration $C'\to P$ with these properties. Mark the edges of $C$ whose images in $P$ are inert.

Let $f:C\to P$ be such an approximation, and suppose its functor on colour fibres $C\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}\{\langle1\rangle\}\to P_{\langle1\rangle}$ is an equivalence. Let $r:E\to P$ be an operadic fibration: a categorical fibration with cocartesian lifts of inert edges, fibre Segal equivalences over the colour projections, and the output mapping-space product property, as in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] with $P$ in place of $L$. Restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Sect}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(C,E).$$
The left side is the full subcategory of coherent sections $s:P\to E$ carrying inert edges to $r$-cocartesian edges. The right side is the full subcategory of coherent lifts of $f$ carrying every marked edge to an $r$-cocartesian edge. Transformations and higher simplices are over the identity in $P$ on both sides. The functor is the specified precomposition, natural under restriction of the target operadic fibration; it preserves the noninvertible transformations as well as their higher simplices. No existence or preservation of limits, colimits, or presentability of the fibres is assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition 2.3.3.6 (approximation), Definition 2.3.3.25 (marking), Theorem 2.3.3.23(1) and Theorem 2.3.3.26. The conclusion is the relative section formulation for an operadic fibration, obtained by taking the fibre of the restriction comparison over the base functor; the marked slice formulation of Theorem 2.3.3.26 gives precisely this relative version. Read online, not archived: WANTED Higher Algebra, section 2.3.3. No Stacks tag treats this infinity-operadic theorem.
